title: Cargo Doors — Installation of a Second Latch Position Sensor at Each Latching Station

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: In-service installation of the second latch position sensor and its bracket at every cargo door latching station, bringing delivered aircraft to the duplicated sensing standard and removing the single-sensor spurious indication.

sections.planning_reason: Aircraft delivered before the production cut-in carry one position sensor per latching station. Any drift in that sensor is indistinguishable from a genuine unlatched condition, and operators have recorded returns to stand and delayed departures on that basis. The duplicated standard resolves the ambiguity by requiring two independent channels to agree, and downgrades a single-channel disagreement from a flight deck warning to a maintenance message.
sections.description: A second position sensor is installed at each latching station of the forward, aft and bulk cargo doors on a bracket plate CAL808635-46 that picks up existing holes in the latching rib assembly D5230135992491. The rib assembly is re-drilled and reamed locally. The new sensor cabling is run on the existing door harness supports and terminated on the second channel of the door warning computing function. Cover plates are attached with screws LN143422-1C and the cabling is retained with ties LN309661K1.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Put the aircraft in the configuration for cargo door maintenance and open the door onto ground support. Remove the latch shrouds and the door lining panels local to each latching station. Confirm that the wear inspection Service Bulletin has been accomplished on this door and that no intercostal is outside the limit. Position the drill jig on the latching rib assembly D5230135992491 and drill and ream the bracket holes. Deburr and restore the protective treatment. Install the bracket plate CAL808635-46 and the second sensor at each station and set the sensor gap to the value in the accomplishment instructions. Run the sensor cable on the existing supports and secure it with ties LN309661K1. Terminate the cable at the door warning connector and do a continuity check of both channels. Install the cover plates with screws LN143422-1C and refit the lining panels and the latch shrouds. Do the cargo door installation and rigging task AMM-T-52-30-13-400-001-A followed by the door operational test, and confirm that both channels agree at every station. Record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to TITAN-88 aircraft up to and including MSN T00113 that have not been built to the duplicated sensing standard. Accomplishment is only permitted on an aircraft on which the latching intercostal wear inspection has already been done and closed, because the sensor datum depends on the intercostal condition.
sections.material_note: Kit K5230-1041-01 contains the bracket plates, the sensors, the cover plates and the fastener set for one aircraft, three doors. Kit lead time is twenty weeks. Removed items are limited to the original cover plates, which are scrapped locally.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled base maintenance visit, or within 48 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.

revision_history.reason: Sensor gap tolerance tightened at step 6; bulk cargo door added to the effectivity
